question: A 62-year-old man is brought to the emergency department by his wife because she thinks he has had a stroke. He has hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus. Current medications include enalapril and metformin. He has smoked 1 pack of cigarettes per day for the past 35 years. His blood pressure is 162/95 mm Hg. A CT scan of the brain shows a lacunar stroke involving the left subthalamic nucleus. The patient most likely presented with which of the following findings on physical examination?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Lacunar stroke involving the left subthalamic nucleus -> Contralateral motor symptoms -> Hemiballismus -> 80% CHAIN: Hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus -> Increased risk of lacunar stroke -> Left subthalamic nucleus involvement -> Hemiballismus -> 75% CHAIN: Smoking history -> Increased risk of stroke -> Lacunar stroke involving left subthalamic nucleus -> Hemiballismus -> 80%
analysis: Based on the clinical presentation of lacunar stroke involving the left subthalamic nucleus in a patient with hypertension and diabetes mellitus, the most likely finding on physical examination would be hemiballismus.
